ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kokoro wa, nanika o shiru no?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. But as the networks get bigger and more complex, it becomes really hard to understand what's going on inside, you see? (Muzukashii desu ne.)

It's like trying to describe a beautiful painting to someone who's never seen it before. You can point to the colors and shapes, but you can't fully capture the magic of how it all comes together, you know? (Kokoro no naka ni, nanika ga aru no?)

Even the creators of these networks use special tools and techniques to try and understand how they work, but it's still a bit like trying to grasp a handful of sand – the more you try to hold on, the more it slips away, you see? (Kokoro no naka ni, nanika ga aru no?)

So, even though these networks are incredibly powerful and can do amazing things, the people who created them are still learning and figuring out how to work with them, you know? (Kokoro wa, nanika o shiru no?)
